extensionAttribute.description: Reports the encryption status of the Time Machine destination. Returns Yes / No / NA / Offline (with cached status if available).
extensionAttribute.scriptContentsMac:
#!/bin/zsh
# Updated by SecurityShrimp 2026 # Time Machine Destination Encryption Extension Attribute # Targets macOS 12 through 26 (Tahoe), Intel and Apple Silicon # CoreStorage is gone on modern macOS — every disk is APFS or HFS+. We # read the destination's APFS encryption status from diskutil's plist # output. The script caches the last-known state in a preference file so # we can still report something useful when the drive is offline.
tmCache="/Library/Preferences/com.capitalone.ds.cof.TimeMachineCheck"
if ! /usr/bin/defaults read /Library/Preferences/com.apple.TimeMachine AutoBackup 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/grep -q "^1$"; then echo "<result>NA</result>" exit 0 fi
info=$(/usr/bin/tmutil destinationinfo 2>/dev/null) mount=$(echo "$info" | /usr/bin/awk -F': ' '/Mount Point/ { print $2; exit }') kind=$(echo "$info" | /usr/bin/awk -F': ' '/Kind[[:space:]]+:/ { print $2; exit }')
if [[ "$kind" != "Local" ]]; then echo "<result>NA</result>" exit 0 fi
if [[ -n "$mount" && -d "$mount" ]]; then encrypted=$(/usr/sbin/diskutil info -plist "$mount" 2>/dev/null \ | /usr/bin/plutil -extract Encryption raw - 2>/dev/null) case "$encrypted" in true|1) /usr/bin/defaults write "$tmCache" status "Encrypted" /usr/bin/defaults write "$tmCache" timestamp "$(/bin/date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)" echo "<result>Yes</result>" ;; false|0) /usr/bin/defaults write "$tmCache" status "Not Encrypted" /usr/bin/defaults write "$tmCache" timestamp "$(/bin/date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)" echo "<result>No</result>" ;; *) echo "<result>Unknown</result>" ;; esac else if [[ -f "$tmCache.plist" ]]; then status=$(/usr/bin/defaults read "$tmCache" status 2>/dev/null) stamp=$(/usr/bin/defaults read "$tmCache" timestamp 2>/dev/null) echo "<result>Offline - ${status:-Unknown} - ${stamp:-Unknown}</result>" else echo "<result>Offline</result>" fi fi
